{"sample_id": "blind-ca705f9c227545879db424dfb174eb30", "theorem": "Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "number_theory", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), so \(m\) is odd and \(p-1=2m\).

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m\). Thus \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\), while \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\). Since the only solutions of \(y^2\equiv1\pmod p\) are \(y\equiv\pm1\pmod p\), it follows that \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Because \(m\) is odd,
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)\mid m\). Conversely, if \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(a\) has order \(2m\), we have \(2m\mid2n\), and therefore \(m\mid n\). Thus \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\), and put \(x=-a\). Then \(a=-x\), \(x^m\equiv1\pmod p\), and
\[
a^{2m}=(-x)^{2m}=x^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Now suppose \(a^n=(-x)^n\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(n\) were odd, then \(x^n\equiv-1\pmod p\). Squaring gives \(x^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid2n\). Since \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\), which would imply \(x^n\equiv1\pmod p\), a contradiction. Hence \(n\) is even. Then \(x^n=(-x)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid n\). Since \(m\) is odd and \(n\) is even, \(2m\mid n\). Therefore \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\), so \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\)."}

（充分性）若 a=0 或 b=0，则当 a=0 时，ab=0·b=0；当 b=0 时，ab=a·0=0。因此 ab=0。

b=(1/a)(ab)=(1/a)·0=0，
所以仍有 a=0 或 b=0。

综上，对任意实数 a,b，ab=0 当且仅当 a=0 或 b=0。"}
